spectre: a ghost; a frightening supernatural figure or apparition
phantom: a ghost or spirit; an apparition seen by the living
apparition: a ghostly figure suddenly appearing; a ghost or spectral vision
dressing-gown: a loose robe worn indoors over nightclothes
waistcoat: a sleeveless garment worn under a jacket; a vest
pigtail: hair gathered and tied in a braid hanging down the back
counting-house: an office where merchants kept their accounts and books
humbug: nonsense; a deceitful or false claim; something not to be believed
forfeits: penalties paid in a parlour game for breaking the rules
great-coat: a heavy, long overcoat worn in cold weather
comforter: a long knitted scarf wrapped around the neck for warmth
cravat: a neckcloth or wide scarf tied at the throat
nightcap: a close-fitting cap worn in bed to keep the head warm
gruel: thin porridge made by boiling oatmeal in water or milk
extinguisher: a cone-shaped device for putting out a candle flame
brawn: meat from a pig's head, boiled and set in jelly
poultry: domestic birds such as chickens, geese, and turkeys raised for food
hearse: a carriage used to carry a copse to its funeral
mourner: a person who grieves, especially at a funeral
shillings: old British coins, each worth twelve pence
workhouses: institutions where the poor were housed and made to work
facetious: playfully joking, often in an inappropriate or annoying way
liberality: generosity, especially in giving money or kindness freely
credentials: documents or qualities that prove a person's identity or worth
ill-will: hostile feeling; bad intent or dislike toward someone
tremulous: trembling or shaking slightly, especially from fear or weakness
livid: bluish-grey in colour; pale with fear or furious with anger
wrapper: a loose garment worn wrapped around the body at home
trifled: treated something lightly or carelessly; played idly with it
shrivelled: shrunk and wrinkled, as from age, cold, or dryness
nipped: pinched or bitten sharply, as by bitter cold
dingy: dirty, dull, and drab in colour or appearance
hooded: wearing or covered by a hood
lamplighter: a person whose job was lighting street lamps each evening
furrows: deep wrinkles in the skin, or long grooves cut in the ground
pounds: units of British money, each worth twenty shillings
bowels: the innermost parts or deepest recesses of something
abroad: away from home; out in the world or in foreign lands
bestow: to give or grant something as a gift or honour
retire: to withdraw or go away to a quieter, private place
quarters: lodgings or rooms where a person lives or stays
endeavoured: tried hard or made an effort to do something
door-nail: a nail with a flat head used on doors; said to be dead
tucker: food, especially a meal, in informal or dialect speech
elder: older, senior in age or rank than another
surplus: an amount left over beyond what is needed or used
brood: a family of young children; a group of offspring
excrescence: an unnatural outgrowth or abnormal lump on the body
resent: to feel bitter or angry at something one considers unfair
crutch: a support held under the arm to help a lame person walk
collars: the upright or turned-over bands at the neck of a garment
tassels: hanging ornaments made of bunched threads or cords
apparel: clothing or garments worn by a person
ponderous: heavy and slow, both in movement and in thought
vigour: physical or mental strength, energy, and liveliness
keenly: with sharp feeling, intense interest, or great eagerness
mournful: sorrowful and expressing grief or sadness
sepulchre: a tomb or burial vault carved into stone
garment: a piece of clothing worn on the body
chattering: rapidly knocking together, as teeth do from cold or fear
gaunt: unnaturally thin and bony, especially from hunger or illness
idle: lazy; not working; or without purpose or substance
wassail: a festive drink of warm spiced ale, drunk at Christmas
